thesis: Centrus is the only NRC-licensed HALEU producer in the U.S. and the only publicly traded pure-play enricher in the West, with $4.5B of backlog to 2040 and a signed $900M DOE HALEU enrichment award. The stock is down ~70% from its high because the equity math got worse: a ~$500M share-and-warrant raise in September 2026, trailing free cash flow of roughly -$164M, and a DOE FY2027 budget that no longer funds the legacy HALEU Operation Contract. At $140 with ~$33.78/share of net cash and 26.5% short interest, it is an asymmetric option on the January 2028 Russian import ban rather than a core holding.

drivers: Piketon and Oak Ridge milestones land on schedule, starting with the first new centrifuge completed by year-end 2026
Roughly $3.0B of contingent LEU and HALEU commitments convert to firm orders as construction progresses
January 1, 2028 expiry of Russian uranium import waivers forces U.S. utilities into domestic SWU, lifting enrichment prices
More commercial HALEU offtake contracts with prepayments, following the Antares Nuclear agreement
Warrant exercises from the September 2026 offering fund expansion without a further primary raise
26.5% short interest amplifies any upside move

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 revenue lands inside the reaffirmed $450–$500M guidance range and capital deployment stays within $350–$500M. The first Oak Ridge centrifuge completes on time and HALEU output scales slowly toward the initial 12 tonnes per year, with full rate after 2030. SWU prices stay firm without spiking. Free cash flow remains negative but funded from the $1.87B cash balance plus offering proceeds. The stock recovers toward the low end of a $218 median sell-side target as execution de-risks.

risks: DOE FY2027 defunding of the HALEU Operation Contract removes ~$0.8B of Technical Solutions backlog in a segment already running a gross loss
Capex overruns or schedule slippage force another dilutive equity raise on top of the ~$500M September 2026 offering
General Matter or Orano scale faster than expected on their own $900M DOE awards, erasing the HALEU scarcity premium
Contingent backlog lapses because financing or construction milestones are missed
SWU unit costs keep rising faster than realized prices, as they did in Q2 2026
Multiple compresses toward net cash plus a modest operating business in a nuclear-sector risk-off move

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings (estimated, after market close) — watch Technical Solutions revenue, capex pace, and contingent backlog conversion
Completion of the first new centrifuge at Oak Ridge, Tennessee — management's hardest near-dated commitment
Release of the Certified for Construction package for the Piketon expansion
Federal FY2027 appropriations determine whether the ~$0.8B HALEU Operation Contract backlog survives DOE's proposed defunding
Russian uranium import waivers expire with no statutory extension mechanism, forcing U.S. utilities to replacement enrichment supply
Targeted start of commercial-scale HALEU production at Piketon

key_risks: Dilution: the September 11, 2026 offering priced ~$500M at a combined $199.64 per share and warrant, adding 500,000 shares, pre-funded warrants for 2,005,513 shares, and common warrants over up to 6,992,382 shares against ~20.45M shares outstanding; share count is already up ~31% YoY
Trailing free cash flow of ~-$163.8M with FY2026 capital deployment guided to $350–$500M; H1 2026 operating cash flow was negative
DOE's proposed FY2027 budget does not fund operation of the HALEU cascade and DOE does not intend to exercise further options, putting ~$0.8B of Technical Solutions backlog at risk

Competition funded on the same terms: DOE awarded $900M each to Centrus, General Matter and Orano in January 2026; per Politico reporting General Matter targets 355 tonnes of HALEU annually versus Centrus's initial 12 tonnes
Roughly $3.0B of the $4.5B backlog is contingent on Centrus actually building the capacity
Weak earnings quality — trailing operating income is ~$0.5M and reported profit leans on investment income; Altman Z-Score ~2.67, Piotroski F-Score 3
Extreme volatility: 85 daily moves greater than 5% in the past year, beta ~1.33, and 26.5% short interest creating gap risk in both directions
SWU and uranium price sensitivity — Q2 2026 average SWU unit cost rose 13% against a 3% price increase
Lumpy quarterly revenue because LEU contracts carry annual rather than quarterly purchase commitments
